claims.claim: Google DeepMind used AlphaProof Code in a four-week project to formally verify key cryptographic guarantees of the Signal protocol and found no new vulnerabilities in the portions examined.
claims.episode_span: formally verify a set of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees, in a proof-of-concept that ran four weeks
claims.source_title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
claims.supporting_quote: Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways.

claims.claim: The cryptography examined protects communications on Signal, Google Messages, and WhatsApp.
claims.episode_span: cryptography that protects communications on Signal, Google Messages, and WhatsApp
claims.source_title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
claims.supporting_quote: It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp.

claims.claim: AlphaProof Code identified known vulnerabilities in older Signal versions and showed those versions could not be formally verified.
claims.episode_span: AlphaProof Code identified them and showed those versions could not be formally verified
claims.source_title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
claims.supporting_quote: when the researchers used AlphaProof Code on older versions of Signal that contain known and long-fixed vulnerabilities, it correctly identified them and showed that the protocol could not be formally verified.

claims.claim: Signal CTO Ehren Kret said DeepMind’s approach expanded formal verification beyond smaller portions of code.
claims.episode_span: Ehren Kret said the approach enabled a significant expansion beyond prior formal verification of smaller portions of code
claims.source_title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
claims.supporting_quote: While prior formal verification focused on smaller portions of the code, Google DeepMind's approach enables significant expansion,” Ehren Kret, Signal's chief technology officer, says in a statement.
